strengths: Addresses a major bottleneck of RKHS-based conditional conformal prediction (Gibbs et al., 2023) by developing an elegant and stable path-tracing algorithm.

Formulates two custom piecewise-linear solution paths (the $\lambda$-path for hyperparameter tuning and the $S$-path for the test score cutoff), resulting in substantial speedups (at least 40-fold) compared to the original binary-search-based optimization.

Successfully extends the method to high-dimensional covariates by utilizing low-rank latent embeddings (e.g., PCA, pLSI, or NN embeddings) and provides robust finite-sample guarantees under estimation errors.

Extensive and diverse empirical validation across multiple domains (molecular graphs, arXiv citation count prediction, and brain tumor MRI) demonstrating consistent conditional coverage with sharper prediction sets.
weaknesses: The computational efficiency relies heavily on the assumption that the 'elbow set' remains small ($|E| \ll n$). While this holds empirically in most tested scenarios, the paper would benefit from a discussion on potential edge cases where $|E|$ grows large (e.g., high noise levels or misspecified kernels) and how the speedup degrades in those cases.

Assumption 2 requires the low-rank projection map $\hat{\pi}(\cdot)$ to be trained symmetrically across the calibration and test data to preserve exchangeability. In practice, achieving this for neural network models can be computationally challenging if model weights have to be updated, which could be discussed more explicitly in the main text.

strengths: Addresses a major computational bottleneck of the RKHS-based conditional conformal prediction framework (Gibbs et al., 2023) by deriving exact solution-path algorithms (both λ-path and S-path).
Establishes solid theoretical foundations, proving piecewise-linearity of the parameter updates and providing finite-sample approximate conditional coverage guarantees under low-rank embeddings.
Proposes a practical extension to high-dimensional regimes by conditioning on learned low-rank embeddings within the RKHS, preventing the curse of dimensionality.
Demonstrates exceptional empirical speedups (40x to 50x) and superior conditional coverage across diverse real-world datasets (molecular graphs, text topic models, and medical images).
weaknesses: Despite the massive speedup, the absolute runtime of the algorithm is still somewhat high for large calibration datasets (e.g., hundreds of seconds on the MRI dataset) compared to standard split conformal prediction, which may limit applicability in ultra-fast online settings.

The method relies on a symmetric embedding map estimation (Assumption 2) across calibration and test sets, which might require re-fitting embeddings when new test points arrive if the embedding maps are not already frozen.

strengths: Addresses a critical bottleneck in kernel-based conditional conformal prediction (Gibbs et al., 2023), providing a practical solution with up to 50-fold speedups.
Well-grounded mathematically, with solid theoretical derivations of the piecewise-linear solution paths (Propositions 1 & 2), monotonicity (Proposition 3), and localized coverage guarantees.
Clever integration with low-rank latent representations to extend the conditional coverage paradigm to high-dimensional regimes.

Comprehensive experimental evaluation across various domains (GNN molecular data, text modeling, CNN medical images) demonstrating consistent target coverage and smaller prediction sets compared to strong baselines.
weaknesses: The algorithmic novelty of path-following in kernel quantile regression is somewhat incremental, as it heavily builds upon existing solution path algorithms (e.g., Li et al., 2007).
Under some sparse data regimes (e.g., the ML topic in Table 2), the coverage variance remains relatively high, suggesting potential sensitivity to hyperparameters or data density.
